questions.stem: What causes refraction when a wave passes from one medium to another?
questions.explanation: Refraction is caused by a change in wave speed as the wave passes from one medium to another. The change in speed causes the wave to change direction if it enters the new medium at an angle to the boundary.

questions.stem: When light passes from air into glass at an angle, what happens to its direction?

options.text: It bends away from the normal
It continues in the same direction

questions.explanation: When light enters a denser medium (like glass from air), it slows down and bends towards the normal. When it enters a less dense medium, it speeds up and bends away from the normal.
